nodes.description: The recurrent heterozygous ATP2A2 missense variant p.(Pro602Leu) replaces a proline in the ATP-binding domain of SERCA2. Expressed in vitro, the mutant pump has lost its ability to transport calcium into the sarco/endoplasmic reticulum. This is the same gene and the same functional class of lesion as in Darier disease, which is the basis for regarding the two as allelic.

nodes.description: SERCA2 sequesters cytosolic calcium into the endoplasmic reticulum of keratinocytes, and this store supports keratinocyte differentiation and, indirectly, intercellular adhesion. Loss of pump activity is inferred to disturb that store in the affected acral epidermis. No study has measured keratinocyte calcium handling in AKV directly, and why the lesion is confined to acral skin, and why it largely spares adhesion here when it does not in Darier disease, is unexplained.

nodes.description: Small suprabasal clefts with acantholytic, sometimes mildly dyskeratotic keratinocytes have been found in some genotyped AKV lesions on step sectioning, and Darier-like cytology including corps ronds and grains in another case. Their absence has long been used to separate AKV from Darier disease, so this node records an inconstant finding that bears on that question rather than a defining feature.
